A high-end Emote mod featuring **R15 character rigs**, **R6 bends**, a wide range of capabilities including model and particle rendering, as well as sound and music playback that ensures the best possible experience for both users and bundle developers. **All currently compiled Minecraft versions will receive future updates.**
<br/>
<br/>

## User Guide

Firstly here is the default keybind for usage.

| Action 			| Default key 	|
| --- 				| --- 			|
| Emote Wheel 	   	| `` ` ``  		|
| Lock Emote 		| `F9` 			|

- Hold down the ***[Emote Wheel]*** key to open the Emote Wheel menu; releasing it will close the menu. Move your mouse to preview emotes, then release the key while hovering over an emote or simply **left click** it to play.

- Moving while playing an emote will cancel it. To prevent this, press the ***[Lock Emote]*** key once to toggle the emote lock.

- **The Emote Wheel features a filtering system**: simply click one of the options on the left to view only the filtered emotes on the wheel.

- You can add your favorite emotes to a favorites list for quick access. While in the menu, simply hover over an emote and press ***[Mouse Middle Button]*** to favorite it. Now you can view it by filtering `Favorites`.

### Commands

| Command | Permission | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/universal-emotes reload` | OP Level 4 | Reloads all bundles and re-syncs every online player |

### Locked Emotes & Settings?

- Some emotes can be locked by the server, which is configured by bundle creators. Depending on their setup, certain emotes may require a specific **OP permission level**, while others might require reaching a certain in game **experience level**. You may encounter these restrictions directly in the Emote Wheel menu.

- If you are a server owner, you can disable the **OP requirement** by enabling the `Ignore animation op level` setting, or disable the in game **experiment level** requirement by toggling off `Require experience level` in the mod's configuration menu. You can access the settings by navigating to Mods from the main menu, locating Universal Emotes, and clicking on its icon **(requires Cloth Config and Mod Menu)**.

- You can also set the level requirements for each rarity.

- If you can't access the in-game settings menu, you can simply edit the configuration files located in the `config/universal-emotes/settings/` folder inside your Minecraft directory. Both **client** and **server** configuration files can be found there.

> **TIP:** Make sure to keep the [JSON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON) syntax valid when editing manually. You can use a tool like [JSONLint](https://jsonlint.com/) to validate your changes if you encounter any issues.

> *You can access other settings and their information in game settings...*

### Bundles & Installation

- Bundles have a size limit of 100 MB and are archived packages in [ZIP format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_(file_format)) that can contain up to 256 emotes.

- Move the downloaded bundle (ZIP) file into the `config/universal-emotes/bundles/` directory inside your Minecraft folder.

> NOTE: While [universal-emotes-packs](https://github.com/theptah/universal-emotes-packs) repository indexing bundle download links is currently available, an in-game bundle browser has not been implemented yet. **Coming soon!**

- **All you need to do is install these packages to the server, when clients connect to the server, it will automatically download the packages in their game.**

## Supported Versions

For now, it only supports the **Fabric** loader but in the future, **depending on your feedback**, I may add support for other loaders.

| Minecraft 		| Java	|
| --- 				| ---	|
| 1.19.x – 1.20.4 	| 17+	|
| 1.20.5 – 1.21.11 	| 21+	|

Requires [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api). [Mod Menu](https://modrinth.com/mod/modmenu) and [Cloth Config](https://modrinth.com/mod/cloth-config) are optional for the settings screen.

## Build Guide

> **INFO:** Any missing JDK toolchains are downloaded automatically by Gradle. Built artifacts will be saved to `./build/libs/` as `universal-emotes-{mod_version}-{game_version}-{loader}.jar`.

Targeted subproject tasks follow the syntax below:

```bash
./gradlew :{version}-{loader}:{command}
```

| Action 	                           | Command 	                                             | Example |
| :--- 		                           | :--- 		                                             | :--- |
| **Build all versions**             | `./gradlew buildAndCollect`                           | `./gradlew buildAndCollect` |
| **Build specific version**         | `./gradlew :{version}-{loader}:buildAndCollect`       | `./gradlew :1.20.1-fabric:buildAndCollect` |
| **Clean build specific version**   | `./gradlew clean :{version}-{loader}:buildAndCollect` | `./gradlew clean :1.20.1-fabric:buildAndCollect` |
| **Clean all build outputs**        | `./gradlew clean`                                     | `./gradlew clean` |
| **List available versions**        | `./gradlew projects`                                  | `./gradlew projects` |

> **TIP:** Append `--stacktrace` to any command above to view detailed error logs if a build fails.

### Project layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main` | Common code: bundle loading, validation, animation, events, networking, server config |
| `src/client` | Client code: emote wheel, rendering, mixins, audio playback, resource pack generation |
| `stonecutter.properties.toml` | Mod version and per-version dependencies |
| `settings.gradle.kts` | List of supported Minecraft versions |
| `stonecutter.gradle.kts` | Active version and cross-version source replacements |

### Adding a New Version

- This project relies on [Stonecutter](https://stonecutter.kikugie.dev/) for multi-version targeting. Version-specific code is managed using `//? if` preprocessor comments, and simple API renames (such as `ResourceLocation` → `Identifier` on 1.21.11+) are resolved via replacements in `stonecutter.gradle.kts`.
- To add support for a new version, register `match("<version>", 'fabric')` inside `settings.gradle.kts` and define the matching `[fabric."<version>"]` table in `stonecutter.properties.toml`.
